truth_boundary: Nine new public proofs and three definitions close two source subobligations: arbitrary feasible initialization (printed p.3 / PDF p.15) and a recursive mean/count summary (printed p.6 / PDF p.18). They are not nine additional numbered book results. Four existing Mean proofs and every prior FTL proof are retained; six validation proofs are not book results. Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. Fix initial c before observations. Lean time t counts observed labels y0,...,y(t-1); predict before observing yt, then update the local state with yt. The algebraic identities hold for all real initial values and labels. Source feasibility requires c in [0,1] and only the strict-past labels yi in [0,1] for i<t; the current and future labels are unrestricted. The state is a mathematical noncomputable exact-real pair (count,value). The count grows; there is no fixed-bit memory, executable implementation or runtime certificate. Strict-prefix equality compares the same fixed c and gives no causality guarantee if an external caller chooses c from future data.
